passage: Honeybees communicate the location of food through a “waggle dance,” in which the angle of the dance indicates direction and its length indicates distance. Researchers long debated whether other bees actually use this information. In one experiment, scientists rotated hives so the dances pointed in misleading directions; recruited bees then searched in the wrong places. The result indicated that bees do rely on the dance rather than only on smell.

steps: Sentence 1 describes the dance; sentence 2 raises a question (do bees use it?); sentences 3 and 4 give an experiment and its answer.
Nothing is abandoned, no two behaviors are compared, and the debate is resolved.
